programme.desc: Nuair tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ a’ cluich geama le Beag is Meanbh, tha e 'g ionnsachadh gu bheil co-roinneadh spòrsail. When Baby Soup Dragan is playing with Small and Tiny, he learns that sharing is a lot of fun.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Air latha fliuch, tha plòigh aig na Losgannan a’ dèanamh dealbh-chluich faileasan. On a rainy day, the Froglets have fun making a shadow show for Bertie and puppet friends.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona airson a bhith na buthaid inbheach is tha i cuideachd airson dòighean-obrach nam buthaidean ionnsachadh do Bhaba. Ach ge-tà, tha i ri dìochuimhneachadh an rud as cudromaiche; gum feum spòrs a bhith aig buthaid òg. Oona wants to be a grown-up puffin and wishes to teach Baba the ways of adult behaviour, but she forgets the most important thing - young puffins need to have fun!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Nuair a lorgas Oona, Mossy agus Baba ugh annasach, tha iad airson coimhead às a dhèidh agus tha iad airson a phàrantan a lorg. Ach feumaidh iad a bhith sgiobalta oir tha an t-ugh ri guar. When Oona, Mossy and Baba find a mysterious egg, they decide to try to find its parents. They have to work fast though, as the egg is close to hatching.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha pàrantan Raghnaill air falbh air chuairt, is tha iad a’ fàgail “Antaidh as fheàrr”, piuthar òg màthair Raghnaill os cionn chùisean. Tha Antaidh coma mu riaghailtean is mu dheireadh thall, tha a’ chlann a’ faicinn cò ris a tha dachaigh gun riaghailtean coltach, fiù ’s Raghnall! Roman's parents are travelling, and they leave 'our favourite aunt', the young and laid-back Roman's mom's sister, in charge. The kids finally experience a house without rules, even Roman!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas air a' chladach ach an lorg iad am facal ùr, 'igloo', an sin? Tha turas 'aba-do-be-dee' eile a' feitheamh airson aon de na h-Abadas, ach cò a thèid air agus càite an tèid iad air an t-sireadh seo? Another 'aba-do-be-dee' adventure awaits one of the Abadas, but who will go and where will their quest take them? The Abadas are at the seaside but will they find the day's word, igloo, there?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Abigail NicÌomhair a’ leughadh An Solas-oidhche san Iarmailt. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh is a dhealbhachadh le Gaetano Dato, agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Abigail Maciver reads An Solas-oidhche san Iarmailt, written and illustrated by Gaetano Dato and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha an Teaghlach Rìoghail air gluasad an ath-dhoras ’s tha Stella airson a h-obair-sgoile a sgrùdadh le Mìcheal agus tha an Rìgh agus a’ Bhànrigh a’ dol a-mach air deit. The royal family have moved next door, Stella wants to revise schoolwork with Mìcheal, and the King and Queen are going on a date.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha caraidean Stella ri tadhal an-diugh agus tha i airson dearbhadh gu bheil iad àbhaisteach – dìreach mar a h-uile duine eile! Stella’s friends visit today, and she wants to prove that they are normal, just like everyone else!

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha tòrr aig Zala ri ionnsachadh mu thrufailean. Le taic bho a nàbaidh, Sara, agus Pùpa, an cuilean, tha i airson trufailean a lorg gus am faigh i air pasta traidiseanta le trufail ullachadh airson na caraidean aice. Zala has much to learn about truffles. With assistance from her neighbour, Sara, and Pùpa the puppy, she goes in search of truffles so that she can prepare a traditional pasta dish with truffles for her friends.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Sebastian a' dol air ais air a ghealladh, taic a thoirt dha Adele leis a' phròiseact aice, chan eil i air a dòigh leis idir, idir. Tha gnothaichean rudeigin fionnar an dèidh sin! When Sebastian goes back on his promise to support Adele with her project, she is not happy with him at all. Things are a bit chilly from then onwards.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: 'S e cò-là breith Timmy a th' ann agus tha an Treud a' cur pàrtaidh air dòigh dha. An toiseach, tha an gnothaich a' còrdadh ris ach nuair a tha e air fhàgail leis fhèin, cò aig tha fios dè thachras...... It's Timmy's birthday, and the flock have thrown a party for him. At first he's delighted by all the attention, but when the flock become distracted and he's left with no-one to play with, he decides to entertain himself.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Abair gu bheil treat air leth aig Abigail – Tost Frangach. An dearbh bhiadh airson brunch le càirdean is caraidean. Abigail has a special treat in store in the form of a tasty french toast snack. It's perfect for that table brunch spread when friends and family visit. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Mach à Seo!
programme.desc: Ramsay visits the Campsies for a fun-filled holiday. Tha Ramsay a’ tadhal air Monadh Chamsaidh son làithean spòrsail.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: Seumas is struggling with the secret of who Rory really is. Meanwhile, Sìleas is forced to take drastic decisions at the mill, including rehiring Boyd. But things begin to unravel as Donald resigns from the family business, and Murdina’s drinking begins to get out of control. Tha Seumas a’ strì leis an rùn-dìomhair mu cò dha rìribh a th’ ann an Rory. Aig a’ cheart àm, tha co-dhùnaidhean mòra aig Sìleas ri dhèanamh aig a’ mhuileann – a bhith a’ fastadh Boyd a-rithist, nam measg. Ach tha cùisean a’ dol ma sgaoil nuair a tha Dòmhnall a’ leigeil seachad a chuid obrach bho ghnìomhachas an teaghlaich agus tha Murdina ann an ceò deoch. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Prois Tartan/Tartan Pride
programme.desc: Ann an 1872 chluich Alba agus Sasainn a' chiadgheam ball-coise eadar-nàiseanta air an t-saoghal, a' cruthachadh sgeulachd aig a bheilbuaidh a chun an latha an-diugh a thaobhfaireachdain, cultar agus eachdraidh an luibsluagh na h-Alba. In 1872 Scotland played England in the first international football match in the world, creating the genesis for a story of emotional, cultural and historical significance that continues to resonate in Scottish society in 2014.

programme.title: Sgeulachd Cogaidh na h-Artaig/Untold Arctic Wars
programme.desc: Deep mistrust exists between the two sides. The Soviet Union threatens with neutron bombs, and Nato deploys missiles in Europe.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Ellie Beaton a’ gabhail a-steach A Miner’s Life agus It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by Ellie Beaton featuring the songs, A Miner’s Life and It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram ciùil air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Chaidh Seirm Celtic Connections a chlàradh ann an ionad Platform ann an Glaschu ann a 2022 le feadhainn den luchd-ciùil as fheàrr bho air feadh a R.A. agus às na S.A. Anns an darna prògram roghainneach seo gheibhear taghadh de cheòl dùthchasach agus traidiseanta bho’n Ciaran Ryan Band, Trials of Cato, Màiri Nic a’ Mhaoilein agus a còmhlan agus Jarrod Dickenson. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Seirm Celtic Connections was filmed in 2022 during the festival in Platform, Glasgow. Appearing are a cross section of musicians from the UK and the US. This programme reflects the diversity of the festival with appearances by the Ciaran Ryan Band, Trials of Cato, Màiri MacMillan and band, plus Jarrod Dickenson. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Art critic Robert Hughes looks at America's majestic landscapes, exploring how artists have contributed to the religious and patriotic connotations of nature.

programme.title: The Making of King Arthur
programme.desc: Poet Simon Armitage traces the evolution of the Arthurian legend through the literature of the medieval age and reveals that King Arthur is not the great national hero he is usually considered to be. He's a fickle and transitory character who was appropriated by the Normans to justify their conquest, he was cuckolded when French writers began adapting the story, and it took Thomas Malory's masterpiece of English literature, Le Mort d'Arthur, to restore his dignity and reclaim him as the national hero we know today.

programme.desc: Simon Bates and Richard Skinner present the pop chart programme, first shown on 6 June 1985. Featuring Gary Moore & Phil Lynott, Kool and the Gang, Propaganda, David Bowie, Duran Duran and Paul Hardcastle.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Film profile of singer and pianist Ray Charles. Featuring Charles in conversation with Charlie Gillett and clips from his 1986 Royal Festival Hall concert and earlier performances.

programme.title: Tina Turner at the BBC
programme.desc: A collection of performances from one of the greatest singers and live performers in modern music - the legendary Tina Turner. This selection of tracks comes from appearances Tina made on various BBC programmes over the years, featuring some of her biggest hits from the 1970s, 80s and 90s.

programme.title: When Tina Turner Came to Britain
programme.desc: Using previously unheard interviews and told in her own words, When Tina Turner Came to Britain is the story of Tina Turner’s 50-year relationship with the UK, also featuring interviews with British musicians and fans who shared her journey. From her first visit alongside Ike Turner, supporting the Rolling Stones in 1966, to her legendary 1983 comeback performance on C4’s The Tube and working with Heaven 17, Tina has always had a soft spot for the UK. With powerful and revealing testimony from the likes of Martyn Ware, Glenn Gregory, PP Arnold, Arlene Phillips and Skin, this one-hour documentary charts Tina’s incredible journey, overcoming challenge after challenge to become the undisputed queen of rock with a little help from her many British friends.

programme.title: Top of the Pops

programme.title: Top of the Pops

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Art critic Robert Hughes looks at America's majestic landscapes, exploring how artists have contributed to the religious and patriotic connotations of nature.

programme.title: The Making of King Arthur
programme.desc: Poet Simon Armitage traces the evolution of the Arthurian legend through the literature of the medieval age and reveals that King Arthur is not the great national hero he is usually considered to be. He's a fickle and transitory character who was appropriated by the Normans to justify their conquest, he was cuckolded when French writers began adapting the story, and it took Thomas Malory's masterpiece of English literature, Le Mort d'Arthur, to restore his dignity and reclaim him as the national hero we know today.

programme.title: Tina Turner at the BBC

programme.title: When Tina Turner Came to Britain
programme.desc: Using previously unheard interviews and told in her own words, When Tina Turner Came to Britain is the story of Tina Turner’s 50-year relationship with the UK, also featuring interviews with British musicians and fans who shared her journey. From her first visit alongside Ike Turner, supporting the Rolling Stones in 1966, to her legendary 1983 comeback performance on C4’s The Tube and working with Heaven 17, Tina has always had a soft spot for the UK. With powerful and revealing testimony from the likes of Martyn Ware, Glenn Gregory, PP Arnold, Arlene Phillips and Skin, this one-hour documentary charts Tina’s incredible journey, overcoming challenge after challenge to become the undisputed queen of rock with a little help from her many British friends.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: A new Netflix documentary follows the final stage of Rafael Nadal's tennis career. The series is the latest high-profile sports documentary made for a streaming platform. Zachary Heinzerling, director of Rafa, outlines how the film was made and the level of access his team received. Minal Modha, senior research director at Ampere Analysis, provides context on the growing business of sports documentaries. In Scotland, Peter Murrell's guilty plea to embezzling funds from the SNP has renewed attention on the reporting that first raised questions about the affair. John Ferguson, political editor at the Sunday Mail, reflects on his own journalism. Laura Kuenssberg explains how she secured the first broadcast interview with Nicola Sturgeon since her estranged husband's conviction. CBS News is facing upheaval following changes in leadership and the departure of several senior figures. The latest developments centre on the dismissal of veteran correspondent Scott Pelley after public criticism of the network's direction. Michael Grynbaum, media correspondent at The New York Times, outlines the story.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: As the World Cup kicks off, who is cashing in and who is paying up? 2026 is set to be Fifa’s most lucrative tournament ever, with billions being earned from TV rights and sponsorship deals, as well as controversially high ticket prices. So how do broadcasters and sponsors make their huge investments pay off? Ricardo Fort helps companies advertise at leading sports tournaments and shares his insights from his time as head of sponsorships at Visa and Coca-Cola. And as streaming giant Dazn tries to change the way the world watches live sport, its head of football rights Pete Oliver explains how new technology is changing viewing habits. Also, Ben Thompson hears from leading sports consultant Tony Simpson at Oliver Wyman about how these big tournaments boost economies and can leave a lasting legacy.

programme.desc: When Chelsea goes to make a coffee, she notices her milk hasn’t been delivered. She reviews her doorbell footage and is shocked to discover a man breaking into her house all while she was asleep upstairs. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows how even fancy apartments are targets for thieves. And Anabela is gobsmacked when she discovers her cat has been stolen, but will turning to social media manage to recover him?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine marvels at a treasure trove of jewellery and coins found by a metal detectorist in Herefordshire, now proudly on display at a museum in the county. Among the treasures is a 5th-century pendant made of rock crystal, a gold ring intriguingly decorated with rosettes and coins bearing images of Anglo-Saxon kings. Hunting for treasure in nearby Leominster are two teams, guided by antiques experts Charles Hanson and Richard Madley. In red are besties Sandy and Chris. Married couple Jo and Dee are in blue. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team considers pouring their money into a Chinese famille rose teapot, and across the antiques centre, the blues are weighing up whether they can afford a silver wine funnel. They are also reminded of a trip to Italy when they spot a Murano glass bowl. But will memories be made at the auction in north Wales when auctioneer Matthew Tong climbs the rostrum to sell their items?

She wants to establish holiday lets and also rehome dogs in need, so Sonali takes her to a sanctuary to find out what it takes to look after the thousands of rescue animals in their care.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Sue Kent are in Water Orton to help Johnny and Jo transform their uneven, overgrown garden, neglected for 60, maybe 70 years, into a stunning blend of rustic French charm and English Victorian elegance. The couple want to keep an old ivy as a central feature, alongside fragrant lavender, honeysuckle and jasmine to attract wildlife. Sustainability is key, with reclaimed brick for raised beds and walkways, and recycled wooden reels repurposed for tables. A gin-and-tonic pergola, cosy seating area and hidden garden nooks will add charm and character throughout the space. Married for 31 years, Johnny and Jo first met when he was a chef and she his manager. Their journey took them to France, raising two boys before returning to the UK. Now retired, they have poured their hearts into restoring a former sweet shop and general store into a home full of character – and they’re ready to do the same for the garden. Can the team bring this historic plot back to life with a modern twist on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high stakes quiz as a team of celebrity TV presenters - Gareth Malone, Stephen Bailey, Mwaka Mudenda and Ore Oduba - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. The bridge has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies, and each player must try to cross by answering questions on different subjects. Once they have each faced the bridge on their own, those who have been successful join forces to face the final crossing, for a chance to take home prize money for their chosen charities.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group B between host nation Canada and Bosnia-Herzegovina at Toronto Stadium. Canada are playing at their third World Cup, having previously appeared in 1986 and 2022, but have yet to win a game. Coached by Englishman John Herdman, they will be looking to their key men such as Bayern Munich’s Alphonso Davies and Juventus forward Jonathan David to finally clinch a victory on the biggest stage of all. Bosnia-Herzegovina qualified through the European play-offs, beating Wales and Italy to clinch their place. They are captained by 40-year-old Edin Dzeko, the former Manchester City striker. This is the first ever meeting between the two teams.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine marvels at a treasure trove of jewellery and coins found by a metal detectorist in Herefordshire, now proudly on display at a museum in the county. Among the treasures is a 5th-century pendant made of rock crystal, a gold ring intriguingly decorated with rosettes and coins bearing images of Anglo-Saxon kings. Hunting for treasure in nearby Leominster are two teams, guided by antiques experts Charles Hanson and Richard Madley. In red are besties Sandy and Chris. Married couple Jo and Dee are in blue. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team considers pouring their money into a Chinese famille rose teapot, and across the antiques centre, the blues are weighing up whether they can afford a silver wine funnel. They are also reminded of a trip to Italy when they spot a Murano glass bowl. But will memories be made at the auction in north Wales when auctioneer Matthew Tong climbs the rostrum to sell their items?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Roo Irvine marvels at a treasure trove of jewellery and coins found by a metal detectorist in Herefordshire, now proudly on display at a museum in the county. Among the treasures is a 5th-century pendant made of rock crystal, a gold ring intriguingly decorated with rosettes and coins bearing images of Anglo-Saxon kings. Hunting for treasure in nearby Leominster are two teams, guided by antiques experts Charles Hanson and Richard Madley. In red are besties Sandy and Chris. Married couple Jo and Dee are in blue. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team considers pouring their money into a Chinese famille rose teapot, and across the antiques centre, the blues are weighing up whether they can afford a silver wine funnel. They are also reminded of a trip to Italy when they spot a Murano glass bowl. But will memories be made at the auction in north Wales when auctioneer Matthew Tong climbs the rostrum to sell their items?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage of the opening match in Group B between host nation Canada and Bosnia-Herzegovina at Toronto Stadium. Canada are playing at their third World Cup, having previously appeared in 1986 and 2022, but have yet to win a game. Coached by Englishman John Herdman, they will be looking to their key men such as Bayern Munich’s Alphonso Davies and Juventus forward Jonathan David to finally clinch a victory on the biggest stage of all. Bosnia-Herzegovina qualified through the European play-offs, beating Wales and Italy to clinch their place. They are captained by 40-year-old Edin Dzeko, the former Manchester City striker. This is the first ever meeting between the two teams.

This is the first ever meeting between the two teams.

She reviews her doorbell footage and is shocked to discover a man breaking into her house all while she was asleep upstairs. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine marvels at a treasure trove of jewellery and coins found by a metal detectorist in Herefordshire, now proudly on display at a museum in the county. Among the treasures is a 5th-century pendant made of rock crystal, a gold ring intriguingly decorated with rosettes and coins bearing images of Anglo-Saxon kings. Hunting for treasure in nearby Leominster are two teams, guided by antiques experts Charles Hanson and Richard Madley. In red are besties Sandy and Chris. Married couple Jo and Dee are in blue. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team considers pouring their money into a Chinese famille rose teapot, and across the antiques centre, the blues are weighing up whether they can afford a silver wine funnel. They are also reminded of a trip to Italy when they spot a Murano glass bowl. But will memories be made at the auction in north Wales when auctioneer Matthew Tong climbs the rostrum to sell their items?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Sue Kent are in Water Orton to help Johnny and Jo transform their uneven, overgrown garden, neglected for 60, maybe 70 years, into a stunning blend of rustic French charm and English Victorian elegance. The couple want to keep an old ivy as a central feature, alongside fragrant lavender, honeysuckle and jasmine to attract wildlife. Sustainability is key, with reclaimed brick for raised beds and walkways, and recycled wooden reels repurposed for tables. A gin-and-tonic pergola, cosy seating area and hidden garden nooks will add charm and character throughout the space. Married for 31 years, Johnny and Jo first met when he was a chef and she his manager. Their journey took them to France, raising two boys before returning to the UK. Now retired, they have poured their hearts into restoring a former sweet shop and general store into a home full of character – and they’re ready to do the same for the garden. Can the team bring this historic plot back to life with a modern twist on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Sue Kent are in Water Orton to help Johnny and Jo transform their uneven, overgrown garden, neglected for 60, maybe 70 years, into a stunning blend of rustic French charm and English Victorian elegance. The couple want to keep an old ivy as a central feature, alongside fragrant lavender, honeysuckle and jasmine to attract wildlife. Sustainability is key, with reclaimed brick for raised beds and walkways, and recycled wooden reels repurposed for tables. This is the first ever meeting between the two teams.

She reviews her doorbell footage and is shocked to discover a man breaking into her house all while she was asleep upstairs. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine marvels at a treasure trove of jewellery and coins found by a metal detectorist in Herefordshire, now proudly on display at a museum in the county. Among the treasures is a 5th-century pendant made of rock crystal, a gold ring intriguingly decorated with rosettes and coins bearing images of Anglo-Saxon kings. Hunting for treasure in nearby Leominster are two teams, guided by antiques experts Charles Hanson and Richard Madley. In red are besties Sandy and Chris. Married couple Jo and Dee are in blue. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team considers pouring their money into a Chinese famille rose teapot, and across the antiques centre, the blues are weighing up whether they can afford a silver wine funnel. They are also reminded of a trip to Italy when they spot a Murano glass bowl. But will memories be made at the auction in north Wales when auctioneer Matthew Tong climbs the rostrum to sell their items?

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: The latest news and weather from BBC News Scotland. Presented by Laura Goodwin.

programme.title: Stormborn
programme.desc: The lands of the north bloom as nearly 24 hours of daylight transform the snow-clad landscapes. Arctic fox clans struggle to raise their cubs on Iceland’s volcanic shores. On Shetland, it’s time for the otter cub to strike out alone, while a lone puffin also searches out a partner. And in the mountains, tiny reindeer calves take their first steps. As the season moves on, orca pods arrive in Shetland to hunt harbour seals, and fledgling seabirds take a leap of faith, plunging hundreds of metres from their clifftop nesting ledges to the ocean below.

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian Hamilton and his guide dog Major visit the town of Alloa in Clackmannanshire. Nestled beneath the Ochil Hills and famous for brewing and glassmaking, Alloa sits on the River Forth, which in the past made the town vital for connecting Glasgow to mainland Europe for trade. Alloa is clinging on to its traditional industries, with one brewer and one glassmaker left in the town. However, Ian finds plenty of interest in this busy community as he takes on a judo champion, visits a successful business on the high street, and hears about some dramatic paranormal events in the area. Ian and the crew also get the opportunity to try some delicious handmade tablet, and Ian grabs the chance to take part in a tasting at Alloa’s last remaining brewery.

programme.title: Wha's Like Us
programme.desc: Sanjeev Kohli takes a humorous look at how films have shown Scots, the Scots character and stereotypes, celebrating some of our most memorable onscreen moments. Are we really as mean, parochial and up for a fight as the movies often make us out to be? Sanjeev examines which Scottish stereotypes have a whiff of truth and which ones should be fed to the Loch Ness Monster. Packed with great film clips from both famous classics and lesser-known cult gems, the programme features contributions from an impressive supporting cast list, including actors Kate Dickie, Clare Grogan, Gary Lewis, Denis Lawson, Alex Norton and Tam Dean Burn. From popular adaptations of Kidnapped and Rob Roy to war dramas such as The Great Escape, from the wily islanders of Whisky Galore to the dark urban humour of films such as Shallow Grave, we look at what stories these films have told the world about us, and what these characters can teach us about ourselves. We eavesdrop on tourists taking in the sights with an Outlander tour, drawn to visit Scotland through our most expensive ever drama production, and we celebrate an unexpected staple of Scottish cinema: Scottish men crying.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: A chance to see some of the early episodes of Still Game (first shown in 2002). It is the middle of a harsh winter and the old boys are frozen beyond belief. In the search to find some heat, are they desperate enough to break the law?

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: With their house in turmoil in the midst of the redecoration, new Latimer Crescent residents Alan and Michelle take refuge from the floor sanding at Beth and Eric’s house. Michelle is keen that they are not going to be a nuisance and tries to get to bed as early as possible, but just as she heads upstairs, Christine arrives bearing rhubarb. Hot on her heels are Cathy and Colin, who turn up with the leftovers from their restaurant meal. And Alan realises that it is not easy to leave the sawdust behind - discovering it in the most inconvenient of places.

programme.title: Janey Godley: Still Got It
programme.desc: Filmed in 2022 at Glasgow's Websters Theatre during her chemotherapy treatment, Janey Godley faces up to her mistakes in a hilarious, touching and scorchingly honest stand-up comedy performance. This show was a landmark moment in her life and career. Time in recovery and isolation gave Janey a new perspective on how she lived her life, on how fragile people can be, and that maybe she does care about what others think of her. Janey Godley passed away on 2 November 2024.

programme.title: America's New Female Right
programme.desc: Layla Wright travels to the USA to meet the influencer women posting antifeminist and other offensive content online.

programme.title: Hunting the Rolex Rippers
programme.desc: More and more luxury watches are being snatched off UK streets. In 2022, there was an estimated 60 per cent increase in watch thefts worldwide. It is now the crime of choice for many criminals, seen as easier and more lucrative than drug dealing. In this documentary, journalist Tir Dhondy gets access, for the first time ever, to the gang members behind the crime. She meets the teenage moped riders snatching watches off the street, as well as a gang leader who runs a team of teenage watch rippers and female watch spotters. Tir also comes face-to-face with the 16-year-old who used a machete to steal singer Aled Jones’s £17,000 Rolex in broad daylight.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: Remarkable people are dedicating their lives to saving Asia's extraordinary wildlife, using ingenious solutions. In Borneo, we follow a sun bear being released back into the wild, and in Java, we see how a breeding programme is saving the Javan green magpie. In Japan, orphaned shark embryos are being raised in an artificial uterus. And off Bali, fishermen are trialling new technology that could stop rare species being caught in their nets. We witness a Nepali police raid disrupting the illegal wildlife trade and also join a 24-hour wildlife rescue team saving Sunda pangolins in urban Singapore.

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to Timor Leste in search of the biggest animal to have ever lived - the blue whale. He also hopes to find the saltwater crocodile, one of the giants of land.

programme.title: Shrek the Third
programme.desc: Second sequel in the popular animated fantasy franchise. Newlyweds Shrek and Fiona face their first marital hurdle when the sudden death of King Harold means Shrek himself is next in line. However, with fatherhood looming, Shrek is reluctant. He decides to try and find the true heir - Fiona's errant, rebellious cousin. But while Shrek and his faithful companions Donkey and Puss in Boots go off in search of the heir, handsome rogue Prince Charming stages a coup at the castle. Featuring the voices of Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen Lillian), John Cleese (King Harold), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Eric Idle (Merlin), Justin Timberlake (Artie), John Krasinski (Lancelot), Ian McShane (Captain Hook) and Amy Poehler (Snow White).

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: At the launch of her highly anticipated skincare product, a wellness business owner suddenly dies from an allergic reaction. But Mervin quickly deduces her death to be suspicious when, despite the presence of peanuts in her throat, the victim didn’t eat or drink anything. Meanwhile, Darlene struggles to train up newbie officer Seb Rose as they investigate an obscure party drug that’s doing the rounds on the island. And tensions run high as Selwyn battles devastating news, while Mervin begins to doubt his own instincts when he uncovers compelling evidence in his mother’s case.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: Planet Sex with Cara Delevingne
programme.desc: Porn is everywhere. But Cara discovers it isn’t all bad. In Spain, she helps make an ethical, feminist porn film. She explores positive role models in gay porn in Germany, boy-on-boy love comics for women in Japan and sensitive, homemade porn in New York.

programme.title: Planet Sex with Cara Delevingne
programme.desc: The idea of gender is becoming more talked about. But what is it, and why does it matter? Cara explores drag with a trans man in LA, discovers a third gender culture in Mexico and experiences a ‘gender swap’ in Spain. Along the way, she confronts her own gender fluidity and masculinity.

programme.title: America's New Female Right
programme.desc: Layla Wright travels to the USA to meet the influencer women posting antifeminist and other offensive content online.

programme.title: Hunting the Rolex Rippers
programme.desc: More and more luxury watches are being snatched off UK streets. In 2022, there was an estimated 60 per cent increase in watch thefts worldwide. It is now the crime of choice for many criminals, seen as easier and more lucrative than drug dealing. In this documentary, journalist Tir Dhondy gets access, for the first time ever, to the gang members behind the crime. She meets the teenage moped riders snatching watches off the street, as well as a gang leader who runs a team of teenage watch rippers and female watch spotters. Tir also comes face-to-face with the 16-year-old who used a machete to steal singer Aled Jones’s £17,000 Rolex in broad daylight.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: Remarkable people are dedicating their lives to saving Asia's extraordinary wildlife, using ingenious solutions. In Borneo, we follow a sun bear being released back into the wild, and in Java, we see how a breeding programme is saving the Javan green magpie. In Japan, orphaned shark embryos are being raised in an artificial uterus. And off Bali, fishermen are trialling new technology that could stop rare species being caught in their nets. We witness a Nepali police raid disrupting the illegal wildlife trade and also join a 24-hour wildlife rescue team saving Sunda pangolins in urban Singapore.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The finals continue with the last four chefs back in the UK, where they take on their biggest task to date.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: It's the semi-finals, and the three remaining designers head to Brighton and Hove Albion's football stadium to transform two hospitality boxes each - one for a player's family and the other for a corporate client. Top fan Norman Cook, aka Fatboy Slim, pops in for a visit, alongside players Georginio Rutter and Fran Kirby. There is a lot to juggle in this tough challenge, and a place in the final at stake.

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: Zoe feels liberated at a ‘Gods and Monsters’ party hosted by eccentric local expats Flick and James, while Dan spirals into a dark place back at the villa. News of their separation unsettles each of the friends as the party takes unexpected turns. The frisson between Zoe and Solomon becomes undeniable. Avery is drawn to Jon, Jacob goes on an unexpected sexual odyssey, and Nat blows up her life. When Zoe listens to what her visions might be telling her, will she go too far?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin sees the warning signs directly spelt out to him at a Merseyside property. Jacqui meets four friends in Suffolk embarking on their first property project. And Dion is in Yorkshire, where he wants to fill a void.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A vulnerable, elderly man sparks an island-wide search for answers, a roadside stop uncovers a lethal switchblade, and airport officers track suspicious luggage.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From Charles Paget Wade's collection of samurai armour in Snowshill Manor to the Harpur-Crewe family's immense natural history collection at Calke Abbey, this episode explores the remarkable world of collectors – and the dedicated National Trust teams working to protect their extraordinary legacies of curious collectibles, rare wildlife and living heritage.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Simon Armitage, Josie Gibson, Ardal O'Hanlon and Adele Roberts take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo enjoys a journey on the historic line from Sarajevo to Mostar, descending 600 metres through the Dinaric Alps, reflecting on the divisions which tour apart the old Yugoslavia.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and Clara Amfo bring you the stories that matter from across the country.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Ruth Vichos are back in the Beechgrove Garden just outside Aberdeen, where the climate has been very mixed over the last few weeks. They assess just how that has affected the crops and blooms. George is in the fruit cage checking for pests and also prunes the Beechgrove fig. Ruth is in her vertical plot, ideal for anyone with a small garden or little space to grow, where she plants a perennial that will give a crop year after year. George plants beans, and there’s a visit to Colin Crosbie’s plot near Dumfries, where he is moving hostas and pruning pulmonaria. There’s also a lifting of the first tatties of the year, grown in a container and kept indoors to produce an early crop.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As summer hits its stride at Longmeadow, Monty Don brings a burst of colour to the Jewel Garden with vibrant annuals, plants out tender veg, and shares some practical advice for tackling greenhouse pests. Arit Anderson visits a striking garden in Greater Manchester packed with clever design solutions and wildlife-friendly planting that comes alive by day and night. In Dorset, Joe Swift explores a much-loved family garden reimagined for three generations. In Essex, a gardener has transformed a shaded, north-facing plot into a lush, lawn-free haven, while in Bristol, a Morris dancer channels movement and rhythm into her planting as she prepares for Gardeners’ World Live in Birmingham.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From the conservation of an apprentice indenture from 1785 that tied a 13-year-old boy to a cotton mill, to the unusual homes of working families at Kinver Edge carved into a sandstone hillside, this episode uncovers the hidden lives of ordinary working people – and follows the teams making sure their stories are never forgotten.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Pantalone is planning the heist of the century – a tasty £12 million in rough-cut diamonds. But if you’re going to hire a bunch of complete clowns to carry out a robbery, and half of them are planning to double-cross the other half, you’ve not just got a recipe for disaster, you’ve actually got the ingredients of a Tarantino Commedia dell’Arte.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Queer
programme.desc: William Lee leads an aimless life in the bars of Mexico City, hanging out with other American expats, indulging in drugs and picking up men. Lacking any kind of real emotional connection, when William meets an enigmatic student named Eugene, he becomes obsessed and begins a desperate, drug-fuelled journey into darkness and self-discovery.

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: In a somewhat misguided attempt to resolve Dennis and Walter’s spiralling competitiveness, Miss Mistry offers thumb wrestling as a solution - but can Walter play fair, or will the situation get out of hand?

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: Animated series. DM must save his reputation and the world when Squawkencluck's artificially intelligent defence supercomputer goes despotically insane.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The heroes are relieved that the loud, threatening voice they can hear actually belongs to a small slug named Zorgoth, who is armed with a megaphone. However, when Zorgoth uses his Orb of Compression to shrink the heroes down to the size of ants, their relief evaporates. They must now embark on a long and dangerous quest, through their picnic items and beyond, to warn the Council before Zorgoth shrinks the entire forest.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: When the heroes quest to stop Balthazar from turning forest folk into household objects, Herbert realises that he can defeat the wizard’s spell by using the magic tricks he has practiced. Blossom is particularly intrigued by Herbert the Peculiar’s tricks, not to mention his stage name, so when Herbert himself is transformed into a table lamp, it’s Blossom the Very Impressive to the rescue!

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: When Boy's school Bobblehead Head Club is closed down due to not having enough members, his siblings help make the boring club more fun.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings come up with a ride worthy of a county fair in the living room.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is a ball boy at an important tennis match, but Frog causes chaos by accidentally filling the automatic ball launcher with oranges that splat the crowd!

programme.title: Submarine Jim
programme.desc: Jim must find the pompom he took by mistake.

programme.title: Odd Squad
programme.desc: An international high-tech organisation run by kids, which investigates all things strange, weird and, most importantly, odd.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: KIDZ BOP perform live, a young Irish dancing world champion shows off his skills and gets the surprise of a lifetime, and Shini takes on a challenge with the stars of this year’s T20 Women’s Cricket World Cup.

programme.title: Hacker’s Ruff Guide to the World Cup
programme.desc: Forty-eight nations are competing in the World Cup, so Race Across the World’s Alfie Watts attempts to name as many countries as possible from flags on footballs being fired at him!

programme.title: Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir
programme.desc: Ladybug and Cat Noir unknowingly face Queen Mayor.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: While falling, Grizzy performs a series of acrobatics that amazes the Lemmings.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: The watch! The mobile phone! The microwave! The vibrating poo platform! Thomas Edison stage diving! It’s all here as Horrible Histories takes a journey through the history of tech.

programme.title: The Next Step
programme.desc: Summer receives a letter offering a life-changing opportunity that would ruin Cleo's plans and wrestles with the decision of whether to follow her heart or stick with Cleo. Meanwhile, Winnie tries to convince Nick to use tap in a routine, but an injury forces her to recruit other dancers who don’t share her passion. And Richelle begins to question her own dance future.

programme.title: This is CBBC!
programme.desc: Tune every day from 7.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the spectacular acrobatic Grapes working together to perform the most difficult structures to perfection.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: It's a windy day, and Bing wants to fly his Hoppity Voosh kite with Flop. And he wants to do it all by himself. Even when Pando arrives and wants to help, Bing insists on doing it his way. When the kite gets caught up in the park bench, Bing realises that there are some times when another pair of hands come in handy.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies wait for tubby toast, then they wait for the Tubby Phone to be answered and finally they wait for the Tiddlytubbies to go to sleepybyes. A boy in Tummy Tales waits to cross a road with his grandad and waits for a bus.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Explore the amazing world around us with baby monkey Tee and his Mum, Mo. Sing along, join in with stories and get ready for some family fun!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato helps Tomato get a rare Golden Snuggybear for his museum from a giant toy capsule vending machine, but Evil Pea traps them inside by freezing the machine and takes the toy for herself! Supertato tries to break free but fails. Determined to escape, Tomato transforms into the Red Roller, whirls around the inside of the machine, breaks the ice and sets them free. Supertato and Tomato surf the resulting wave of toy balls to catch up with Evil Pea and rescue the Golden Snuggybear.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Nicky are sleeping over at Sula's house, but Bing has forgotten Hoppity! The wind causes a branch to make a scratchy noise that terrifies Bing, who isn't very comforted by Sula's fairy rhino. Amma phones Flop, while Sula, Nicky and Bing play 'Nicky tickles' as they wait. Flop arrives, bringing his sleeping bag and Hoppity so they can all sleep over.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo have to make sure Dot doesn’t see her present before her birthday party. But that’s easier said than done when Dot becomes an unstoppable present-hunting machine.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have made a song. They enjoy playing for others but wish they had a chance to see how they perform together. Duggee explains that they can if they make a music video, which tells a story. There is a lot to prepare beforehand, such as lights, costumes and glitter, and as they prepare, we are immersed into Enid’s dream, where she gives a star performance in her own eclectic music video! The Squirrels are taught to practice their dance moves before filming, to pick the perfect location and to try and put something unexpected into the video. After lots of collaboration, creativity and fun, the Squirrels finally get to watch their own music video and are thrilled at the results.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey wants to know why Dad is always bossing her around!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey must find a way to play postman and the ground's lava without squabbling with Bingo.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters are adventure-seeking explorers who soar around the planet fixing environmental problems caused by Grandmaster Glitch!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: After Benjamin gets lost in the woods, Peter and Lily give him a map to help him find his way home. But when the map falls into Mr Tod's hands, the rabbits must work together to stop the fox from finding their home.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. The Octonauts venture into a dangerous red-hot lava tube to rescue a teeny-tiny water bear who doesn't seem to mind the heat at all!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Learn how much fun counting can be with the Numberblocks - a fun-loving group of numbers who work together to solve problems big and small.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. Letters A and I pair up to make the new and exciting sound AI, but will it help them on their journey?

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piris plan a trip to Tippety Top to see the famous southern lights but lose each other in an ice fog. When Nugget thinks she sees a monster, Pancake proves to be an unlikely hero.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift make a new friend with an awesome roar, Steggy the Dinosaur! Together, they visit Tincy in the Sing Song Forest for a dinosaur song.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula have a penny each for the surprise machine in Padget's shop. Sula gets the silver rhino she wanted, so Bing is convinced he will get the alien he wants. When the surprise machine delivers his capsule, Bing is upset to discover that the alien is not inside.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘milk’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. There’s white milk, pink milk, baby milk and banana milk. We snuggle up for bedtime milk and even enjoy some mighty milk and monster milk! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu upsets Elodie when she laughs at an involuntary noise she makes.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri has to overcome her jealousy when everyone gives Lou presents.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button compete in their own Froggie sports day.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a shop filled with bric-a-brac where they watch a lady putting brightly coloured cardboard stars next to some items in the window display. She leaves the box of stars on the counter and goes into a back room. The Twirlywoos come out and take stars from the box, putting them next to as many different things as they can, until all the stars are used up. The lady comes back to discover that every item in the shop now has a star next to it! The Stop-Go Car visits the boat and brings the Twirlywoos some red, yellow and blue coloured blocks. The Twirlywoos decide to line them up, taking turns to place one colour next to the other. They make a long line of blocks which stretches across the boat, finishing outside Peekaboo's hole. While the Twirlywoos are busy celebrating, Peekaboo peeps out and knocks the end block, causing it to fall into the one next to it, until they all collapse, domino-style! This is repeated several times, with the Twirlywoos setting up the blocks and Peekaboo knocking them down again. In the end, the Twirlywoos chase after their rings, and Peekaboo takes the blocks into the hole.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin spends the day at his friend's school. They have lots of fun in the classroom, meeting the school dog and eating pizza. Meanwhile, it is Tumble Ted's first day at school and Mr Tumble pretends to be the teacher.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. Chip sings a heartfelt song about being a potato. Though he can't do many physical things, he is proud of who he is.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po enjoy Tiddlytubbies Songtime. Then it is time for Teletubbies Songtime. The Teletubbies sing solo before singing all together.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Joseph, Baani, Jean, Amber, Amelia, Luke and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are dollies which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding a safe, baby appropriate dolly inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun nursery rhyme ‘Miss Polly had a Dolly’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children craft hanging stars from twigs and colourful string, learn British Sign Language signs for twinkle, star and world, then sing and sign Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Food stylist Rob introduces the Fact Pack to edible flowers and explains how they can be used to make food look and taste exciting.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Baby rhino Maisha is in a bad mood, but her friends help her feel better. Hamza spots some fantastic colobus monkeys in the trees and searches for clues to find the elephants.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes must reclaim their yummy drops from the Beetrootsaurus.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Indy and Rusty play Mums and Dads, they can't agree on who should go to work, so they part company. Indy has a hard time finding a babysitter, while Bluey makes Rusty her baby.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are admiring everything Duggee has grown in his vegetable garden, especially his crop of giant carrots, when they hear a noise. They investigate and find the Rabbits busy preparing for the Carrot Solstice, the day when the sun is at its highest. On this day, they gather round Carrot Henge to celebrate the glory of this humble vegetable. Trouble is, the Rabbits need to go and get ready – but who will look after the carrots? The Squirrels volunteer, so off the Rabbits go. Looking after the carrots seems easy at first, and Norrie arranges tasks for everyone. Betty skillfully organises the queue while Roly is on toilet duty. And then, disaster strikes. Worm pops up and eats part of Carrot Henge. Duggee is dispatched to fetch one of his own giant carrots to fill the gap. As time ticks on with no Duggee in sight, the place gets busier, and the sun is nearly at the top. Will Duggee fix the Henge in time, or will Carrot Solstice be ruined?

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Red and Blue meet Yellow and have fun colouring the seaside. Discover the colours around you.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Jasiri finds out some fascinating frog facts! Rory and his son Sandy hop like frogs to the local lochside and make a pond in their garden. Ferne visits an aquarium to meet some amazing amphibians including poison dart frogs. Also, we find out why frogs' place in the food web makes them so important to the balance of the planet.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Amanpreet challenges her sister Amrit to a biking competition to see who can cycle around the bike track the fastest. But who will win? The bikes get really muddy, so Amanpreet takes charge of giving them a good clean and has some splashy fun with the hosepipe too. Later, she makes delicious shortbread for the whole family, including a special biscuit for little brother Arjun.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Diellza's family comes from Kosovo. She makes a traditional recipe of stuffed peppers. Diellza has lovely colourful ingredients for her stuffed peppers, such as spring onions, sweetcorn and grated carrot. She also uses cooked rice, chopped tomatoes, parsley, garlic puree and paprika for seasoning. This yummy filling is stuffed into her peppers and placed in the oven to be cooked for her friends. To accompany her meal, Diellza serves her friends a traditional Kosovan drink made of yoghurt and water called kos. Will they enjoy her drink, and will they guess what the special ingredient is?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today’s episode, Maddie explores how our body works. She visits a children’s hospital to find out what happens when we have an X-ray. She meets James, who has broken his arm, as well as a radiographer. We see what happens when we have an X-ray and learn how the X-ray machine takes a picture of the bones inside our body before saving the picture on a special machine. Next, Maddie heads to a factory where they make socks in lots of different colours out of yarn. Maddie uses her slow-motion camera to give us a special view when the sock-turning machine sucks in the socks and flips them out the right way around. They look like wiggly snakes!

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Guide dog Kika uses her super sight to help Dr Amit and his friend Alana play a game of sound tennis. Kika tries not to chase the noisy balls at the sports centre.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet the largest amphibians in the world, the Chinese giant salamander. They watch these secretive creatures emerge from their underwater rock shelters and use their amazing, superfast strike to grab their breakfast. Next, they meet a pair of Alaotran gentle lemurs. These beautiful creatures live in only one place in the wild – on the island of Madagascar. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona, Baba and Mossy babysit a little egg and help find its mama and papa.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes has written a brilliant song, but his guitar string is broken, so he can't play it. Yukee decides to surprise Stripes by enlisting his garden friends to sing the song to him. The trouble is, they can’t find the right pitch to sing the song in!

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are having a camping sleepover in their garden, but things take a mysterious twist when Dad discovers someone, or something, has been eating the vegetables in his patch. Maddie and Triggs turn super sleuths and conclude this is the work of a veggie monster!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels notice that Happy looks and seems different – he is frowning, his smile is upside down, and he’s wearing new trainers! When they check in on him, Happy is frustrated, but he can’t seem to identify where his frustration is coming from. They turn to Duggee for help, who uses his feeling cards to explain an array of feelings to Happy. All the Squirrels help by relaying their past experiences and the feelings that they evoked.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One finds a friendly furball, two of them tickle Two and soon Numberland is full of fun and fluffies! Have fun counting and learning how to make sevens with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. S is feeling a bit sad but T, A and P are there to help and before long, everyone is tap-dancing. T has no tea, A has too many apples, but S is sagging so the others want to help. P pops in and they try some word magic - perhaps a comforting pat or a big musical number? This episode introduces the letters S, A, T and P and the words sat, pat, tap and taps.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin meets Rheagan on the slopes to take part in her skiing lesson. George joins in the snowy fun too! Meanwhile, Mr Tumble helps Tumble Ted get ready for a big adventure of his own. There's snowy activity in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words coat, helmet and ski slope.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po have their favourite things. The bag, the hat, the scooter and the ball all magically swap places and become mixed up.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back to the time of iberomesornis - a bird that lived in the forests of Spain 127 million years ago. His mission is to find some blue feathers belonging to the bird to replace the one he and Hatty accidentally lost back at the museum. Along the way he takes to the skies with one of the largest flying pterosaurs that ever lived. But will he succeed before the museum opens?

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: The Fantastics find themselves up against the grown-ups in a big match! They think they’re going to win easily, but how will they respond when the grown-ups play surprisingly well?

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: Series for young children that celebrates lots of different amazing machines. In this episode, motorcycle rider Grace Webb shows off three amazing machines that are all made to clean! First, Grace helps to clean a canal in a litter collection boat and shows off a brilliant ocean cleaner, and then she helps to clean an ice skating rink on an ice cleaner!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Henry has some brilliant bouncy fun with Mummy and sister Sophie!

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: A Portuguese man o' war washes ashore; the Octonauts need to reunite him with his legion.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter accidentally leaves the burrow's door open in a storm, it floods! As the family searches for shelter, Peter soon realises there truly is no place like home.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After hearing a strange sound, the Squirrels turn to Duggee to help identify its source. They learn about sound waves, and that you can listen for different qualities in the sounds, such as if it’s loud, quiet, high or low. Describing the sound can help you work out where it’s coming from, so Duggee lets the Squirrels close their eyes as they listen to sounds and make their guesses.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Daphne is very excited to show off her clean teeth at the clinic’s Dental Day.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato shows the Grape Kids how to camp Supertato-style, but Evil Pea arrives and wows them with her ice camping. Before long, the Grape Kids need to be rescued by Supertato.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings go for a bumpy ride in the radio-controlled car. Weasy is worried his things will get damaged, so he draws no-traffic zones with chalk - but the ducklings don't respect the 'rules of the road' imposed by their father.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: It’s secret agent time when Mojo and Bo think Didi the tractor is up to something fishy. But can the two supersecret spies follow her without being spotted?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey wants to know why Dad is always bossing her around!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey must find a way to play postman and the ground's lava without squabbling with Bingo.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: When Mara calls Pearl sensible, she wants to prove how fun she is. With her eye off the ball, Pearl starts to make medical mistakes. Can she be a fun doctor?

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Andy and Jen are on an epic adventure to discover what the dinosaurs of Dino Island get up to at night. When Andy loses his gizmo and gets lost in the dark, a friendly velociraptor comes to his aid. Along the way, Andy spots a T rex and narrowly avoids being stomped on by a herd of Alamosaurus, who are protecting their eggs.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi spots an old family photo, where she looks small next to her dads. Wanting to seem more grown up, she wishes to be taller - and suddenly she is! It’s fun at first, but she soon realises she misses being carried by her dads and the closeness of doing things together.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: It’s been raining, so JoJo wants to get outside and splash in the puddles. Isaiah arrives for his play date with JoJo, but Isaiah wants to stay inside and read his science books. Gran Gran suggests they compromise, but what is a compromise? Gran Gran has a plan: they can use the puddles outside to do a science experiment inside. They use timers and the sun to track the edge of the puddle and find out how long it takes for a puddle to disappear.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck give Moon painting lessons after being inspired by a trip to the art gallery.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: When Major Clanger decides that the Soup Dragon must be fed-up with dishing up soup for them all every day, he invents a machine to collect the soup instead. But when he takes some soup without even asking the Soup Dragon, he overfills the machine and it gets stuck in the doorway. Only with the help of the Soup Dragon can it be freed, and as it is freed, it explodes everywhere. Perhaps sometimes it is best to leave things as they always were.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: BaBa peers into a puddle and sees themself reflected back. MeMo explains that it’s BaBa’s reflection. At the Play Tree, they look in a toy mirror and pull funny faces - it also comes in handy at Yummy Time, when they need to clean their faces after a messy meal of spaghetti. On the Lullaby Lake, they see the sky reflected in the water as they travel to the Bay of Books.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Series for young children about a magical place inhabited by a community of toy characters that care for each other and have fun together. The Pontipines count to three. Makka Pakka's trumpet makes a funny noise. There is something wrong with it. Igglepiggle and Upsy Daisy visit Makka Pakka and help him discover a stone stuck in his trumpet. Makka Pakka gives Upsy Daisy the stone as a present, and everybody joins in the dance at the gazebo.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: England cricketers Katherine and Nat Sciver-Brunt read a Bedtime Story about a triangle trying to fit in.
